# Engine: host-aware run lock and process registry (KAN-88)

## What to build

graph-manager will run some graph-execution runs inside a Docker container (a "sandbox"). The engine in the container writes the run lock (`<runDir>/lock`) and the process registry (`<runDir>/pids/<pid>.json`) into the workspace, which the server also sees. PIDs from another PID namespace mean nothing on the server: today a `--resume` or `graph-execution clean` typed in a graph-manager terminal would see the sandbox's PIDs as dead, take the lock over and SIGTERM unrelated process groups. This slice makes both host-aware:

- The lock gets a third line, the host name (`os.hostname()`; inside a container that is the container's hostname). Old one- and two-line locks are read as "this host".
- A lock written by another host is never stale: `acquireLock` refuses it with `LockError`, `lockHolder` reports it as held. The one exception: when `GRAPH_EXECUTION_TAKE_LOCK_FROM` equals that host, the lock is stale and taken over (graph-manager sets this after it checked that the old container is gone).
- Each registry record gets a `host` field. `reapOrphans` skips records of another host (never signals them); records of the host named in `GRAPH_EXECUTION_TAKE_LOCK_FROM` are deleted without any signal.
- `graph-execution/api` exports `readLock` (pid, token, host, foreign) and the env name constant, for graph-manager.

Engine only (`packages/graph-execution/src`). No UI. Spec: `docs/prd/sandboxes.md` (Decisions rows "The engine records the host name…" and "A run started in a sandbox is resumed in a sandbox…"; Requirements → Engine bullets 2, 3 and 6).

This feature is built in parallel with two other features (KAN-89 run options, KAN-87 reviewers) that also edit `state/state.ts`. Keep the edits additive and local to the lock / registry code.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `packages/graph-execution/src/state/state.ts` (lines 160-226) — `LOCK_FILE`, `LockError`, `isAlive`, `heldLocks`, `parseLock`, `lockHolder`, `acquireLock`. This is the whole lock implementation you change.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/state/processes.ts` (whole file, 220 lines) — `ProcessRecord` (lines 16-29), `recordProcess` (65-72), `trackProcesses` (90-112), `isRecord` (114-128), `reapOrphans` (172-220).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/state/paths.ts` (whole file) — env-name constants (`RUNS_ROOT_ENV`, `RUN_ID_ENV`) and `RUN_ENV_UNSET` (the variables agents and gate commands must NOT inherit).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/api.ts` (whole file, 14 lines) — the public surface graph-manager imports (`graph-execution/api`).
- Callers that must keep working unchanged: `cleanup/scan.ts:91` and `:122` (`lockHolder(dir)` → `kind: "live"` when defined), `launch/preflight.ts:224-231` (`assertNotRunning`), `runner/run.ts:158` and `:218` (`acquireLock`), `runner/run.ts:220` (`reapOrphans(runDir, { log })` on resume), `suite/orchestrator.ts:161,203,206`, `cleanup/execute.ts:22`.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/state/state.test.ts` (lines 122-189) — the `acquireLock` tests to extend (they write lock files by hand with `writeFile(lockFile(), ...)`).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/state/processes.test.ts` (lines 1-120) — the registry tests: `record(pid, owner)`, `recordPath(pid)`, `spawnGroupLeader()`, `deadPid()`, `alive()`, `waitGone()`.

## Patterns to follow

Current lock parsing and takeover (`state/state.ts:177-215`):

```ts
function parseLock(text: string): { pid: number; token: string | undefined } {
  const [first = "", second] = text.split("\n");
  return { pid: Number(first.trim()), token: second?.trim() || undefined };
}
export async function lockHolder(runDir: string): Promise<number | undefined> {
  const { pid } = parseLock(await readFile(path.join(runDir, LOCK_FILE), "utf8").catch(() => ""));
  return Number.isInteger(pid) && pid > 0 && pid !== process.pid && isAlive(pid) ? pid : undefined;
}
// in acquireLock:
await writeFile(file, `${process.pid}\n${token}\n`, { flag: "wx" });
...
const { pid } = parseLock(await readFile(file, "utf8").catch(() => ""));
if (Number.isInteger(pid) && pid > 0 && pid !== process.pid && isAlive(pid)) {
  throw new LockError(`run ${name} is locked by the running process ${pid}; wait for it or stop it`);
}
await rm(file, { force: true });
```

Env constants live in `state/paths.ts`:

```ts
export const RUN_ID_ENV = "GRAPH_EXECUTION_RUN_ID";
export const RUN_ENV_UNSET = { [RUNS_ROOT_ENV]: undefined, [RUN_ID_ENV]: undefined, GRAPH_EXECUTION_READY_FILE: undefined, GRAPH_EXECUTION_TASK_NAME: undefined } as const;
```

`RUN_ENV_UNSET` is spread into the env of every agent (`providers/spawn.ts:113`) and gate command (`validate/commands.ts:46`); its type is used as `typeof RUN_ENV_UNSET & { PWD: string }` so adding keys is safe.

Errors: `LockError` (already exported from state.ts) with a lowercase, actionable message.

Test pattern: write the lock file by hand, e.g. `await writeFile(lockFile(), \`${process.ppid}\nabc\nother-host\n\`)`, and set/unset `process.env.GRAPH_EXECUTION_TAKE_LOCK_FROM` inside the test (restore it in `afterEach` / `finally`).

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/state/paths.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: add, below `RUN_ID_ENV`:
  ```ts
  /** Internal (graph-manager): the host whose run lock and agent records this process may take over (its sandbox container is gone). */
  export const TAKE_LOCK_FROM_ENV = "GRAPH_EXECUTION_TAKE_LOCK_FROM";
  ```
  and add `[TAKE_LOCK_FROM_ENV]: undefined,` to `RUN_ENV_UNSET` (agents must never inherit it).
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run typecheck -w graph-execution`

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/state/state.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `import os from "node:os";` and `import { TAKE_LOCK_FROM_ENV } from "./paths.js";` (check paths.ts does not import state.ts — it does not).
  - `export const lockHost = (): string => os.hostname();`
  - `parseLock(text)` returns `{ pid, token, host }`: third line trimmed, `host: third?.trim() || os.hostname()` (old locks = this host).
  - `export interface LockInfo { pid: number; token?: string; host: string; foreign: boolean }` and
    `export async function readLock(runDir: string): Promise<LockInfo | undefined>` — the raw content of `<runDir>/lock` (undefined when missing or the pid line is not a positive integer); `foreign` is `host !== os.hostname()`. No liveness check.
  - A private helper `takeOverAllowed(host: string): boolean` → `process.env[TAKE_LOCK_FROM_ENV] === host` (an empty or unset variable never matches).
  - `lockHolder(runDir)`: for a foreign lock, return its pid unless `takeOverAllowed(host)` (then undefined); never call `isAlive` for a foreign pid. Same-host behaviour unchanged.
  - `acquireLock`: write `${process.pid}\n${token}\n${os.hostname()}\n`. On `EEXIST`, parse; when the lock is foreign:
    - `takeOverAllowed(host)` → `rm` it and retry (stale);
    - else throw `new LockError(\`run ${name} is locked by process ${pid} on host ${host} (a graph-manager sandbox); resume it from graph-manager\`)`.
    Same-host logic unchanged (dead pid or our own pid not held → stale).
  - Update the doc comments of `lockHolder` / `acquireLock` (content is now `<pid>\n<token>\n<host>\n`).
- **GOTCHA**: the release function compares only the token line; keep it so (`parseLock(...).token`).
- **GOTCHA**: `os.hostname()` must be read at call time, not cached at import (tests may not change it, but keep it simple and correct).
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-execution -- state/state`

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/state/processes.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `ProcessRecord` gets `/** os.hostname() of the CLI that spawned it; absent in records written before KAN-88 (= this host). */ host?: string;`
  - `trackProcesses` sets `host: os.hostname()` in the record it writes (import `os from "node:os"`).
  - `isRecord` accepts `host` when absent or a string.
  - In `reapOrphans`, right after a record is parsed and before `ownerAlive(rec)`:
    ```ts
    if (rec.host !== undefined && rec.host !== os.hostname()) {
      // Another host's agents (a graph-manager sandbox): their pids mean nothing here. Never signal them.
      if (process.env[TAKE_LOCK_FROM_ENV] === rec.host) rmSync(file, { force: true });
      continue;
    }
    ```
  - Update the `reapOrphans` doc comment with this rule.
- **IMPORTS**: `TAKE_LOCK_FROM_ENV` from `./paths.js`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-execution -- state/processes`

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/api.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: add `readLock`, `lockHost` and `type LockInfo` to the existing `./state/state.js` export line (line 5), and add a line `export { TAKE_LOCK_FROM_ENV } from "./state/paths.js";` (or append it to the existing paths.js export on line 6). Additive only.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run build -w graph-execution && npm test -w graph-execution -- api`

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/state/state.test.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT** in `describe("acquireLock")` (and a new `describe("readLock")`):
  - a new lock has three lines and the third is `os.hostname()`;
  - an old two-line lock of a live other pid (`process.ppid`) is still refused (existing test keeps passing) and `readLock` reports `host === os.hostname()`, `foreign: false`;
  - a lock `999999\nabc\nother-host\n` (a pid that surely is not alive here) is NOT stale: `acquireLock` rejects with `LockError` mentioning `on host other-host`, the file is unchanged, and `lockHolder(dir)` returns `999999`;
  - with `process.env.GRAPH_EXECUTION_TAKE_LOCK_FROM = "other-host"`, `lockHolder(dir)` is undefined and `acquireLock` takes it over (the new file's first line is `process.pid`, third line `os.hostname()`); with `= "someone-else"` it is still refused;
  - `readLock` returns undefined for a missing file and for `"abc\n"`.
  - Restore `process.env.GRAPH_EXECUTION_TAKE_LOCK_FROM` (delete it) in a `finally` or `afterEach`.

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/state/processes.test.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT** (inside the existing `describe.skipIf(win32)("process registry")`):
  - "never kills the agents of another host": spawn a group leader, write its record with `host: "other-host"` and a dead owner (`deadPid()`), call `reapOrphans(dir, { graceMs: 100 })` → returns `[]`, the process is still alive, the record file still exists.
  - "TAKE_LOCK_FROM drops another host's records without signals": same setup, `process.env.GRAPH_EXECUTION_TAKE_LOCK_FROM = "other-host"` → `reapOrphans` returns `[]`, the process is still alive, the record file is gone. Clean up the env var.
  - "a record of this host (host field set) is reaped as before": record with `host: os.hostname()` and a dead owner → killed, as the existing test.
  - "trackProcesses writes the host": extend the existing trackProcesses test (around line 120) to expect `host: os.hostname()` in the written record.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `<runDir>/lock` is `<pid>\n<token>\n<hostname>\n`; old formats still parse (as this host).
- [ ] A foreign-host lock is never taken over or reported free, unless `GRAPH_EXECUTION_TAKE_LOCK_FROM` equals its host.
- [ ] `reapOrphans` never signals a record of another host; with `TAKE_LOCK_FROM` equal to that host it deletes the record silently.
- [ ] `graph-execution clean` / `scan` see a foreign lock as `kind: "live"` (via `lockHolder`), so they keep that run.
- [ ] `GRAPH_EXECUTION_TAKE_LOCK_FROM` is in `RUN_ENV_UNSET`.
- [ ] `graph-execution/api` exports `readLock`, `lockHost`, `LockInfo`, `TAKE_LOCK_FROM_ENV`.
- [ ] Tests pass: `npm test -w graph-execution -- state/`

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run build -w graph-execution
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm test -w graph-execution -- state/ cleanup/ api
npm test
```

Known environment failure, not yours: `packages/graph-execution/src/cli.test.ts` "exits 2 at startup when --provider claude is not on the PATH" fails wherever a real `claude` is installed next to `node`.
